items.title: Ray Brown interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, AZ, April 16, 2000
items.q: And then the © Fillius Jazz Archive -3- headliners at the Downbeat, the next club, was Billie Holiday and Art Tatum.

ctx.x: Okay. I arrived in New York after a day and a half train trip. And I had my luggage which was one suitcase, and my bass. I had been on a train. And I got off the train, I got on a subway, and I went up and got off at 168th and Amsterdam. And my mother’s sister, my aunt, lived on Amsterdam and 166th. And I carried my bass and bag down the two blocks, and then she lived up on the — there was no elevator, it was a walk-up. She lived on the third floor. And I went up there and she had told my mother that if I came to…

headliners at the Downbeat, the next club, was Billie Holiday and Art Tatum. Not too shabby. And then the next club was Coleman Hawkins and he was playing with a rhythm section of Denzil Best, Al McKibbon and Thelonious Monk. And he only showed up on Saturday night and played “Body and Soul” and left again. But they had his name on there, and people would wait for him, you know they’d say, “Did he show up?” “No.” And whenever his car drove up they would come out of all the clubs and rush over there just to hear…
